column5: The service worker cache is never purged on logout and no authenticated route carries a directive that would keep it out of the cache
column6: next.config.ts enables the PWA with cacheOnFrontEndNav true and aggressiveFrontEndNavCaching true and passes NO runtimeCaching override - no exclude and no buildExcludes - so the library defaults govern what is written to CacheStorage and front-end navigations are cached aggressively by explicit configuration. Authenticated routes are server rendered with personal data in the payload - orders - wallet - addresses and profile - and the headers() block in next.config.ts sets only security headers plus caching for sitemap robots and the xsl - a search for no-store and no-cache and private across that file returns nothing so no private route is marked uncacheable. Nothing in the application ever clears the cache: a search across src for caches.delete - caches.keys - CacheStorage and serviceWorker unregister returns no results. handleLogout at src/helpers/auth.ts:656-684 clears the auth and cart and recentlyViewed slices and deletes two cookies and two localStorage keys and never touches CacheStorage. Whatever the worker cached during a signed-in session therefore stays on the device indefinitely after sign out.
column10: Shared or public device with the PWA service worker registered - which is the production default since register is true and disable applies only to development.
column11: 1. Sign in on a shared device and visit account pages such as orders and wallet so those navigations are cached. 2. Sign out. 3. Inspect CacheStorage in devtools application tab for the cached route payloads.
column12: Signing out purges the caches that hold personal responses - and private routes are additionally marked so they are never written to a shared on-disk cache in the first place.
column13: No purge happens at all and no route is marked uncacheable so cached personal payloads remain on the device after sign out.
column14: Personal order - wallet and profile data can remain readable on a shared device after the customer signs out - and because it is same-origin any script running later in that browser profile can read it too. This compounds issue 41 which covers the same failure for localStorage and issue 3 which covers the token.
column15: Clear the relevant caches on logout with caches.keys and caches.delete and add that to handleLogout alongside the existing cleanup. Separately mark authenticated routes uncacheable - a Cache-Control of no-store and private for /my-account and /cart in the headers() block - and pass an explicit runtimeCaching or exclude configuration so the defaults cannot silently widen what is stored. NOTE the generated sw.js is gitignored and node_modules was not installed so the exact default cache rules could not be inspected from this repository - the configuration and the absence of any purge are what is verified here.

column5: Three cookies including the precise location of the previous user survive logout for a year
column6: The application writes five cookies - access_token and user in src/helpers/auth.ts - userLocation in src/components/Location/LocationSelector.tsx:278 and src/helpers/events.ts:88 - market in src/helpers/market.ts:19 and homeCategory. handleLogout deletes exactly two of them at src/helpers/auth.ts:675-676 - user and access_token. userLocation and market and homeCategory are left in place and setCookie applies a default expiry of 365 days at src/lib/cookies.ts:20 so all three outlive the session by a year. userLocation is the privacy sensitive one: its UserLocation shape carries lat and lng as precise numbers plus placeName and placeDescription and countryCode - so the previous account exact chosen location and its human readable description stay on the device readable by any script and sent to the server on every subsequent request. This is the same shape of defect as issue 41 which enumerated the localStorage keys - the storage medium and the fix differ so it is recorded separately rather than folded in.
column10: Shared or public device where one person signs out and another uses the browser afterwards.
column11: 1. Sign in and set a delivery location so userLocation is written. 2. Sign out through the account menu. 3. Read document.cookie or the devtools application tab.
column12: Session scoped cookies are removed on logout - leaving only values that are genuinely device scoped and defensible such as a language preference.
column13: userLocation with precise coordinates plus market and homeCategory remain with a one year expiry.
column14: The next user of a shared device inherits the previous person location - and can read their chosen place name and description. The stale market cookie also silently scopes the new session catalogue to the previous user market until it is changed.
column15: Delete userLocation and homeCategory in handleLogout alongside the two cookies already removed. Decide deliberately whether market is device scoped or session scoped and document the choice. Consider storing only the country code rather than precise coordinates if the ETA feature does not need exact lat and lng.
